question: Is it permissible for an unmarried woman to shave her head?
asked: A sister who is single and not getting married asks: am I allowed to shave my hair off? I will wear a hijab, don't worry.
answer:
This is an area where we have an explicit hadith, and there are a number of traditions in this regard. Of them is the hadith in Sahih Bukhari: our Prophet ﷺ was bari', freed himself (bari' means "I don't want anything to do with this"), freed himself from two types of ladies.

Number one, the lady who wails over the dead. Wailing over the dead is something that, inshallah, is not really practiced that much anymore, even though some cultures still do it. Wailing is when somebody dies, and ladies in particular raise their voices and chant certain things in a rhythmic fashion: "How are we going to live? Who will take care of us?" This is a type of wailing that was prohibited. As for crying and expressing grief, this is all halal. Wailing is a specific type of crying that especially incorporates haram phrases in it. So the Prophet ﷺ said: I have nothing to do with the lady who does this, and the lady who shaves her head off. Because that was something that the priestesses of old and the ladies of Jahiliyyah did.

So this is one hadith. The other hadith, in Tirmidhi: the Prophet ﷺ forbade a lady to shave her head. This is explicit. So because of this, most of the madhahib say that it is haram. Unless, obviously, there's always an exception for what? Medical. The Shari'ah always comes with this. Any cancer, something of this nature: obviously, no scholar says that it's haram in that case. Obviously.

But the default: one group of scholars, and this is the majority, says it is haram, because the hadith is explicit. And a smaller group of scholars, I believe the Shafi'is and whatnot, said that the default is that it is makruh for the one who is single. As for the one who is married, then it is going to be unconditionally makruh. But for the one who is single... Their reasoning is as follows: this is something Allah has blessed the beauty of a lady with, and so if she is married, then she should beautify herself for her husband. But they said if she's not married, then the strength of the hadith goes down in her case, and so if she wishes to do it, then it is not haram, but simply makruh. It's better to avoid. Both madhhabs say it's better not to do it; the ikhtilaf is: is it haram or is it makruh?

As well, there are a number of narrations from our tabi'un and tabi' al-tabi'in, not from the Prophet ﷺ, but these are early scholars, who said: Allah has honored women with long hair and men with beards. So the point being, this is something that Allah has honored, so then why should we ruin that honor? So the default, we should say, and I say to this sister: no, you should not do so.

However, it is authentically narrated that our mother Aisha, after the era of our Prophet ﷺ, cut her hair to shoulder length, and that was something that was atypical; the Arabs of that time would have very long hair. And it is authentically narrated that she would cut her hair and make it short. So from this we can gather that cutting the hair, even to a short extent, is something that is completely permissible, and it is something between the husband and wife, however she wishes to change or model her hair, as long as shaving is not done, unless it is for a medicinal purpose.

As for other types of hair, and I've gotten a lot of questions about, you know, the eyebrows, inshallah that's a separate question. But for this question, **the default is that no, she should not be encouraged to completely shave the hair, but she may trim it if she wishes.**
